why_relevant_to_dlys_system: The fixed D-Lys block provides cationic and hydrophilic function. The second block X is intended to provide complementary hydrophobic cohesion. Within the aromatic domain (F, W, Y), higher side-chain hydrophobicity indicates a stronger hydrophobic driving force for self-association or core formation, which complements the hydrophilic D-Lys segment.

The fixed D-lysine block provides cationic, hydrophilic character. The second block X is intended to provide complementary hydrophobic cohesion. Within the non-aromatic hydrophobic-conformational domain, hydrophobicity is the primary driving force for hydrophobic self-association and is explicitly preregistered as a main ranking axis with direction higher.

After fixing the cationic D-lysine block, the second block X can contribute to non-repetitive packing and spatial occupancy. Side-chain volume is a mature descriptor for side-chain scale and is preregistered as a secondary material cohesion/space-filling axis with direction higher, subject to redundancy audit against hydrophobicity.

Beta-branching is a geometric constraint on side-chain packing and is associated with beta-structure preference. The domain guidance explicitly states that beta-branching is not an automatic benefit and that if it enters primary ranking, the only acceptable direction is absence. This descriptor helps distinguish candidates by side-chain geometry within the non-aromatic domain.

The fixed D-Lys block provides cationic/hydrophilic delivery function. A second-block X with negative side-chain charge (D, E) may electrostatically interact with or partially neutralize the D-Lys cationic character, whereas neutral or positive side chains preserve the fixed cationic function. This descriptor directly quantifies charge compatibility with the D-Lys block.

measurement_target: presence of a primary amide group in the side chain
why_relevant_to_dlys_system: The domain guidance identifies neutral side-chain amide chemistry (Asn, Gln) as an auditable hydrogen-bonding functional class that is distinct from hydroxyl, thiol, and carboxylate side chains. This descriptor distinguishes amide-containing candidates from other polar candidates without relying on non-discriminative HBD/HBA counts.

Within the same or similar polar functional-group background, side-chain volume provides a mature, reproducible measure of side-chain reach and spatial occupancy. This complements the fixed D-Lys block by allowing comparison of interaction reach and steric accessibility among candidates with different side-chain sizes.
